summary: Discovery call focused on Penguin AI's PLG onboarding needs: quick time-to-first-token, free credits for experimentation, and criteria for moving to Dedicated or Private. Key constraints: latency for interactive chat, data residency questions for EU users, and cost per 1k tokens. Agreed immediate next step: Redwood to send quickstart + credits and an SE-led technical onboarding session.
meeting_header: Date: 2025-09-04 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Location: Zoom
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Samir (Penguin): Hey Alex, Samir here. Lina, Diego and Hannah from Penguin.
[00:10] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya here, I'm the technical lead on the SE side. Jon from developer advocacy as well.
[00:15] Alex: Great, high level today: we'll walk quickstart, show how to get first token fast with our hosted API, and talk through when customers choose Dedicated vs Private. Any must-cover items?
[00:25] Samir: Main thing for us is time-to-first-token and making sure engineers can try without long procurement. Also curious about cost and the freebies you mentioned earlier.
[00:32] Priya: Perfect. I'll do a brief demo of a cURL+SDK flow, call out streaming, and then we can cover security and tenancy options.
[00:40] [00:40] Priya: So first, sign-up is self-service, you get free credits for new orgs. We usually issue a promo credit bundle that lasts 30 days, enough to run ~200k tokens of small chat messages depending on model.
[00:55] Lina: That's helpful — is the credit manual or auto-applied when we sign up?
[01:00] Alex: We can auto-apply for you once you confirm the org domain, or you can redeem a code I send. Most PLG teams prefer the code so they can share internally.
[01:10] Samir: Ok send the code. Diego will want to run some smoke tests.
[01:15] Priya: Quick demo: here's a minimal curl against the Redwood hosted endpoint — note the API key header, model param, and streaming flag.
[01:25] Priya (speaking demo): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_KEY" -d "{\"model\":\"redwood-7b-chat\",\"input\":\"hello\"}" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
[01:40] Jon: SDKs are available, we have examples for Node, Python, Go. The Node quickstart repo is about 6 files and gets you to first token in under 5 minutes if you have an API key.
[01:52] Hannah: Nice — how reliable is streaming? We need interactive latency under 200ms for some flows.
[01:58] Priya: For short responses we typically hit 100-150ms p95 in our hosted infra in us-east for our medium models; heavier models are longer. There's also batching and prefix caching; for interactive chat we recommend enabling the incremental streaming response.
[02:15] Lina: What about data retention — will user prompts be stored? We have EU residency concerns.
[02:21] Alex: By default hosted stores logs for telemetry but we have options: you can opt out of data retention for production orgs, or go Dedicated/Private where logs stay in your VPC. For compliance we integrate with KMS for customer-managed keys.
[02:35] Samir: If we start with hosted, can we later migrate to Dedicated without changing app code?
[02:40] Priya: Yes — API is consistent. You can pin model versions and redirect traffic to Dedicated. There may be config changes for keys/endpoint, but SDK calls are the same.
[02:50] [03:00] Diego (joined): Sorry, late - had a quick call. Can you catch me up?
[03:05] Alex: We're demoing quickstart and credits, Priya covered typical latencies and migration path to Dedicated/Private. We were about to show a small streaming snippet.
[03:15] Diego: Quick Q: our main blocker is cost predictability. Do you provide cost breakdowns per token and tooling to control spend?
[03:22] Jon: Yes, Console gives token-level breakdown, route-level dashboards, and you can set quotas or alerts. Dedicated also has reserved pricing to smooth unit cost.
[03:32] Lina: Also curious about embeddings — we use Pinecone today. Do you provide embedding endpoints and how does storage integrate?
[03:38] Priya: We provide embeddings endpoint; you can use any vector DB. We'll show example of batching embed requests and a sample flow pushing to Pinecone. We do not host your vector index unless you opt for a managed add-on.
[03:50] Samir: Any blockers for us to try in 24 hours?
[03:54] Alex: No blockers. If you sign up, redeem code I send, your engineers can run the quickstart and get a first token in minutes.
[04:00] [04:00] Priya: Demo caveat: some transcription may have mis-typed product names above — people often say "redwood dedicate" or "K-V cash" in calls — the real names are Redwood Dedicated and KV cache.
[04:12] Hannah: Thanks for the note, ha.
[04:15] Priya: Technical note on streaming: if you need consistent p95 under 200ms we recommend: deploy a lightweight local retry layer, keep prompt windows small, and use the smaller chat model family for latency-sensitive paths.
[04:30] Samir: For security, we need SOC 2 type II and ISO27001 docs and SSO integration.
[04:36] Alex: We have SOC 2 report, ISO paperwork, and SAML/SSO via identity providers; I'll attach the security pack in the follow-up email.
[04:45] Lina: About model selection - are the models open weights or proprietary? We want to fine-tune at some point.
[04:51] Jon: We offer curated open models and some Redwood-verified variants. Fine-tuning or instruction-tuning is supported via private deployments or Dedicated depending on the model. We can discuss the workflow in the SE session.
[05:02] Samir: Can we run a small benchmark — like 10k tokens across chat prompts — and get latency and cost estimates?
[05:08] Priya: Yes, we usually run a pilot benchmark; I can push a small harness and you can run it with the credits. Alternatively we can run it on our side if you share the prompts and expected load.
[05:20] Diego: For the EU residency piece, does Dedicated guarantee data stays in EU?
[05:25] Alex: Dedicated lets you pick regions and keeps data in customer-assigned regions; Private (VPC) is the strictest for residency.
[05:32] [05:32] Priya: Quick practical: I'll paste a sample Node snippet in the notes: const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY}); const stream = await client.chat.stream({model: 'redwood-chat-7b', messages: [...]}); stream.on('token', t => process.stdout.write(t));
[05:48] Hannah: That helps. Any known gotchas?
[05:50] Priya: Watch for tokenization mismatches if you mirror prompts across models; also quantization differences affect perf for on-prem.
[06:00] Samir: Sounds good. Who will be the point person from Redwood for the trial?
[06:04] Alex: I'll be AE and primary contact for trial logistics; Priya will run the onboarding and bench. Jon will provide SDK samples. Marta (CSM) will check in mid-pilot.
[06:16] Samir: Great. We'll likely start with the hosted quickstart to unblock product and then evaluate Dedicated for prod.
[06:24] Diego: One more: do you have usage quotas or rate limits on the free credits?
[06:28] Alex: We have soft rate limits on trials to prevent abuse, but they're higher than typical dev traffic. If you need burst capacity we can raise them during pilot.
[06:36] [06:36] Priya: I'll also include a tiny troubleshooting checklist: common errors, how to rotate keys, and how to enable customer-managed KMS.
[06:48] Hannah: Perfect.
[06:50] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps.
[06:52] Alex: I will send quickstart, promo credits code, security pack and a calendar invite for the 30-min SE onboarding. Priya will prepare SDK snippets and a small benchmark harness. Diego to confirm security checklist items.
[07:08] Samir: Sounds good thanks everyone.
[07:12] Diego: Thanks, logging off to sync with infra team.
[07:15] Alex: Thanks all, chat soon.
[07:18] [End of recording]
